amendments.made: 2026-10-04, after the first run on NBA data only (before any NHL/NFL/MLB demand data existed)
amendments.trigger: One NBA title-clinch event: the market resolved to 99.95%, so the odds-move size and odds level were far outside anything in training; the regression extrapolated to an absurd order and wiped out M3's result (-69% of opportunity, almost entirely from that one event).
amendments.change: (a) M3's odds features are clipped to the range seen in training (no extrapolation); (b) when the market has resolved (odds after the move >98% or <2%) M3 uses the class-only forecast, because a resolved market carries no magnitude information.
amendments.not_changed: event set, windows, demand proxy, economics, M0-M2, metrics, inference. Both the original-spec and amended results are reported.

amendments.made: 2026-10-04, during data QA of the NHL pipeline, before any NHL/NFL/MLB three-merchant result was computed
amendments.trigger: Clear game-driven moves were labelled 'off-court news' because the rule required the move to START during the game; in thinner markets (NHL) odds drift a little before puck drop and finish repricing hours after the final horn.
amendments.change: Signal classification (an input to M1-M3): a game explains a move if >=50% of the move happened inside [tip - 1h, tip + game length + 3h], using only prices up to the emission hour and only games that had finished before emission.
amendments.not_changed: detection thresholds, denoising gates, the scenario engine and its metrics.
